component.name: Workspaced
component.summary: Several Google Workspace accounts, signed in at once

description.p: Workspaced keeps several Google Workspace accounts signed in at the same time, one keystroke apart, each in its own isolated session — no more signing out of one account to check another, and no more incognito windows.

Pick an account in the rail and its apps open as tabs under it: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, Keep and the rest. Accounts you are not using sleep on their own, holding their place with a small unread feed instead of a full Gmail, and wake the moment you switch back. New mail in a sleeping account arrives as a notification.

ul.li: Any number of Google accounts, each with its own cookie jar
Per-account tabs across the Workspace apps, Alt+1–9 to switch
Idle accounts sleep and are polled for unread mail; one click wakes them
On Omarchy, every app is repainted in the system theme as it changes
Meet links open per account in a Chromium window, or the default browser when none is installed
mailto: links land in the right account's Gmail

description.p: A session that Google drops no longer strands a tab on a marketing page: the view is sent back to the sign-in page, aimed at the app it was showing, so signing in again lands where the old session was. The ad-tracking hops in Google's sign-out journeys stay inside the app instead of being handed to the system browser, where content blockers break them, and a signed-out account's unread check backs off from every two minutes to every fifteen.

A page whose web process dies — a renderer crash the sandbox cannot keep quiet — is now loaded again automatically, up to three times in two minutes. A tab that keeps dying is marked with a red ring in the sidebar, and clicking it reloads; reloading goes through WebKit itself rather than a script, which a dead process cannot run.

On systems where no Chromium-family browser is installed — inside a Flatpak sandbox, among others — Meet links and calls now open in the default browser instead of doing nothing, with the account they came from named in the URL.
